tagline: From a spa town's old fairground to the Pee Dee mound.
intro: The trail comes into Ellerbe from the east on Millstone Road, turns north on US 220, the road through the state's prime peach-growing country, where fruit stands open by the road in season, and then takes NC 73 for about 11 miles. Indian Mound Road, which turns into Town Creek Mound Road at the Montgomery County line, runs on to Town Creek, and NC 731 carries on into Mount Gilead.
Somewhere along the way the guidebook points out the farm of Andre the Giant. The wrestler owned land at Ellerbe for many years, and his ashes were scattered there after he died in Paris in 1993.

moments.title: Ellerbe
moments.text: Scottish settlers held a fair here every May and November, so the place was the Fair Grounds until W. T. Ellerbe built a spa at the springs nearby and the town took his name.

moments.title: Town Creek Indian Mound
moments.text: On a low bluff where Town Creek meets the Little River, the state has rebuilt a temple on the Pee Dee's platform mound, where clans gathered to settle debts and feast on new corn.

moments.title: Mount Gilead
moments.text: A textile town incorporated in 1899, where a downtown mural honors the Pee Dee and a loblolly pine in the community garden grew from a seed that went around the moon.
